_comment: Sovereign Ecosystem Framework Manifest. Classifies every repo path into framework, seeded or user. Default rule: any path not matched by a pattern below is class 'user' and is never touched by upstream updates.

framework.description: Owned by upstream. Safe to offer updates. The Sovereign may apply or decline each file individually.
patterns: Council Chamber/AI Interface/AI Interface Knowledge Map.md

seeded.description: Shipped by upstream once. Personalized by the Sovereign after install. Never auto-updated. Updates available only by explicit request using --force-seeded.
seeded.note: MODULES.md calls these 'onboarding-generated' or 'runtime-created' surfaces. They arrive from upstream as starting points and are immediately owned by the Sovereign.
paths: Council Chamber/Codices/Ṣāḍguṇya - Six Strategies of External Engagement.md
Council Chamber/AI Interface/AI Interface Engagement Calibration Log.md
Council Chamber/AI Interface/AI Interface Readiness Snapshot.md
Council Chamber/AI Interface/Sovereign Command Refresh Log.md

explanation.Humor Codex.md: Ships as a seeded starter per v2.11.0. Personalization is a named onboarding step. Upstream changes are reference material only.
explanation.Primer.md: Pre-personalization the file is framework-class boilerplate. Once the Sovereign edits it for their own session state it becomes seeded. The script treats it as seeded by default because there is no reliable automated way to detect the personalization boundary.
explanation.Sovereign Command.md: Runtime-created surface per MODULES.md. Owned by the Sovereign from first use.
explanation..claude/settings.json: Ships pre-wired with the four Foundation hooks via $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, so it works without personalization. Sovereigns add their own permissions and hooks after install, so upstream changes are advisory, not applied directly.
explanation.Governance Principles.md, Watch Register: Governance instruments that accumulate the Sovereign's own entries (principles, watches, baseline rows). Shipped as lightly-seeded shapes, owned by the Sovereign from first use.
explanation.hooks/*.sh: Hook scripts ship from upstream but are configured per-installation (vault path, regen commands). Applying an upstream update blindly would overwrite local configuration. The Sovereign applies hook updates manually after reviewing the diff.

user.description: Never touched by upstream. Sovereign-created content and runtime state. The default class for any path not matched above.
examples: Council Chamber/Pending Plans/** (except Index conventions, which are framework)
Any path not matched by framework or seeded patterns
user.note: Council Chamber/Pending Plans/Index.md is framework-class because it follows a conventions-driven structure upstream maintains. Individual plan files are user-class.

framework_pattern_notes.Council Chamber/Skills: All Skill directories are framework EXCEPT sync-state.json (seeded) and the Sovereign Sync skill itself (framework, added by this release). Skill content that gets modified during use (like sync-state.json) is seeded.
framework_pattern_notes.Council Chamber/AI Interface: Knowledge Map and Operating Charter are framework. Runtime logs and calibration surfaces are seeded because they accumulate session-specific data.
framework_pattern_notes.Getting Started: Entire directory is framework. Onboarding guides are upstream-maintained reference material.
framework_pattern_notes.UPDATES: Entire directory is framework. The append-only update record and its index are owned by upstream.
framework_pattern_notes..hidden: Framework. Hidden blessings ship from upstream. The easter egg log lives at the repo root as EASTER_EGGS.md.
framework_pattern_notes.Council Chamber/Codices: Mixed. Most codices are framework. Humor Codex is seeded (personalized during onboarding). Ṣāḍguṇya codex is seeded (doctrine the Sovereign may adapt to their own sovereignty practice).
framework_pattern_notes.Primer.md: Treated as seeded. Pre-personalization it is boilerplate; post-personalization it is the Sovereign's own session handoff surface.
framework_pattern_notes.Council Chamber/scripts/hooks: Seeded, not framework. Scripts arrive from upstream but require installation-specific configuration. The Sovereign applies hook updates by reviewing diffs, not via --apply. Two exceptions, both listed explicitly in the framework file list: floor-gate-selftest.mjs and hooks-selftest.mjs. They are the positive controls on the guards, they take no installation-specific configuration (each resolves the vault root exactly as the guard it tests does), and they are the files in this directory that must arrive from upstream unmodified. A test the Sovereign has quietly weakened is worse than no test.
framework_pattern_notes..github/workflows: Framework. The clean-clone verification that fires every guard on every push and weekly on a schedule. It exists because v3.3.0 shipped a deletion guard that had been read and never fired, and nothing in this repo was verified on any push, so there was no moment at which that could have been caught. A Sovereign may add jobs. Removing the guard jobs removes the only thing standing between a broken guard and a silent ship.
